title: Stale-policy delta caused cross-region serving on incompatible model variant
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: A customer-facing outage where requests from several Dedicated tenants were routed to an incompatible, heavily-quantized model variant in the EU region. The result was elevated error rates and token-level truncation for some responses, plus latency spikes as retries cascaded across regions. This ticket covers detection, root-cause fix, and remediation steps applied in production.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a tenant scoped to dedicated capacity with policy pinning to model: redwood/gpt-x-1.2
2) Simulate a policy delta event by applying a routing policy update via the control plane (+policy-ttl=5s) while issuing a steady stream of short-chat requests (seq len ~ 64)

3) Observe router decision logs: stale policy snapshot is used on the edge router for ~7-20s leading to routing to redwood/gpt-x-1.2-quantized-eu which lacks the required tokenizer vocabulary and has different response length handling
4) Confirm failure modes: inference errors (model returned 500-like errors), truncated outputs, and increased client retries causing cross-region latency
root_cause: A race during policy propagation: the control plane applied a merge that changed tenant-level preference ordering. The edge router consumed an intermediate policy snapshot due to a stale in-memory policy cache with a decay window longer than expected. Additionally, model-compatibility checks were overly permissive for quantized variants, so the router treated the quantized EU variant as compatible even though it lacked the correct tokenizer/variant mapping for that tenant.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed: force-refresh endpoint for router policy cache to flush stale snapshots (hotpatch v1.31.2)
Roll back the control-plane policy merge for the affected tenants to the previous known-good ordering (rollback 2026-02-19 04:12 UTC)
Immediate canary: pin affected tenants to hosted fallback tier while we validated variant compatibility across regions
monitoring_changes: Added router metric: policy_snapshot_age_seconds (histogram) and alert when > 5s
Model-compatibility check added to route decision path with metric: route_incompatible_variant_count
Dashboards updated: per-tenant route outcome heatmap and cross-region retry waterfall
postmortem_summary: We identified a short-lived propagation race combined with permissive compatibility rules as the cause. Fixes included: stronger compatibility validation, reduced effective policy cache decay window, and a force-refresh control endpoint. The incident lasted ~35 minutes for the most impacted tenants; mitigation reduced additional customer-facing errors within 6 minutes of detection. We will pursue a longer term: atomic policy apply semantics and schema-level variant compatibility enforcement.
followups: ENG-121210: Implement atomic policy apply (coordinated commit across control plane and routers)
ENG-121211: Enforce tokenizer/variant compatibility during model onboarding in the catalog
PM-4321: Customer outreach and credits for impacted tenants
DES-412: Add a console visualization for policy propagation lag per-region

notes: This incident primarily impacted Dedicated tenants with strict model pinning and regional routing preferences.
Quantized variants require explicit tokenizer/variant mapping — this constraint will be codified in the model catalog validation pipeline.
Consider reducing default policy cache decay window from 30s to 3s for high-churn customers as a guardrail.
